cf.title: Stale hash entries when reusing an auxiliary resource owner

input.subject: Stale hash entries when reusing an auxiliary resource owner

verdict_reasoning: The bug is real and nobody disputes it, and a committer who knows the area asked for the v4 design. Two fixable design points survive: standards-compat-1 (which part of v4 goes to stable branches) and standards-compat-2 (what ResourceOwnerReset() checks when resources are still held). Neither stops the idea, so no level fails.

brief.title: Clear stale hash entries so resource owners can be reset and reused
brief.problem: Sorting and bulk release leave stale entries in a resource owner's hash table, but ReleaseAuxProcessResources() makes the auxiliary owner reusable without clearing them. On reuse, old entries can be released a second time, or insertion can loop forever because no slot is free. The author traces the bug to b8bff07daa8.
brief.proposed_design: v4 adds a public ResourceOwnerReset() that restores an already released owner and its descendants for reuse and keeps their storage. Auxiliary-process cleanup now uses it. ResourceOwnerSort() clears moved source slots during compaction, and bulk release clears each retired hash entry before its release callback, so reset needs no full-table clearing pass.
user_visible_surface: New C API function ResourceOwnerReset(), callable after all three release phases, which resets an owner and its child owners for reuse.
src/backend/utils/resowner/README documents the new reset operation.
test_resowner test module gains new SQL-callable test functions.
author_claims: Without the fix, a reused auxiliary owner can release old resources twice or hang in ResourceOwnerAddToHash().
The v2 and later regression tests fail promptly with duplicate-release errors when only the fix is reverted, instead of hanging.
In microbenchmarks, clearing during sort and release costs little, except at 16,384 resources (about 240 vs 256 microseconds).
Clearing the full table in reset (option B) grows with the earlier peak, up to about 67 microseconds at a 65,536-entry peak.
pgbench -S showed no consistent throughput change (-1.60% and +0.54% in two runs).
brief.thread_state: Andres Freund asked for a generic reset helper and for clearing in ResourceOwnerSort(), and Rahila Syed asked for benchmarks and plans a detailed review. The author answered with benchmarks and v4, and nobody has replied to v4 yet.
unclear: v1 says "Backpatch-through: 17", but v4 adds a public API, and the thread does not say what goes to stable branches.
The thread does not say whether the new public API is meant for back branches or only for master.
The material does not say what ResourceOwnerReset() asserts or does when resources are still held.
Benchmarks cover one resource kind and one pgbench workload. Nobody measured workloads with many hashed resources per transaction.
The thread does not say how this interacts with Rahila Syed's proposal to release all three phases in one call.

objections.title: Stable-branch target, but v4 adds a public API to resowner.h
objections.failure_scenario: If v4 is back-patched, an extension built against a new minor release can call ResourceOwnerReset(). That extension then fails to load with an undefined symbol on a server still running an older minor of the same major version. Packagers and users find out at load time, after the upgrade order goes wrong.
objections.argument: The CommitFest entry targets "stable", and v1 said "Backpatch-through: 17". v4 adds a new exported function and changes the semantics of the generic release path, as Andres asked in message #4. No message says which part is meant for back branches. A committer would likely want a minimal fix for 17 and later, such as clearing slots in ResourceOwnerSort() and bulk release, and the new API on master only.
objections.author_must_show: Which part of v4 goes to stable branches, and can the back-branch fix work without adding ResourceOwnerReset() to resowner.h?

critic.reasoning: The CommitFest entry targets stable and v1 said "Backpatch-through: 17", but v4 adds an exported function. No message says which part goes to back branches.

objections.title: "Reset" borrows the MemoryContext verb but not its contract
objections.failure_scenario: An extension author knows that MemoryContextReset() frees what the context holds, and calls ResourceOwnerReset() on an owner that still holds buffer pins or locks. In a build without assertions, the owner is reused and those resources are no longer tracked. The leak shows up later as a pin or lock that is never released.
objections.argument: Message #5 names the function by analogy with MemoryContext. But the README hunk says all resources must be released first, so the verb means something else here. The material does not say whether the function errors, asserts, or does nothing when the owner still holds resources, or when release has not finished. For a public API, a committer would likely ask for a name or a check that makes misuse fail loudly in production builds.
objections.author_must_show: What does ResourceOwnerReset() do in a build without assertions when the owner or a child still holds resources or has not finished all three release phases?

critic.reasoning: The material does not say what ResourceOwnerReset() checks when resources are still held. A demand for a production-build check goes beyond existing practice, because ResourceOwnerDelete() has the same precondition and enforces it with assertions only.

refuted.title: Every new resowner field must also be handled in ResourceOwnerReset
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a field to ResourceOwnerData, such as a counter or cached pointer, and updates create and release but not ResourceOwnerReset. The auxiliary owner, or any extension owner that uses the new API, is reused with stale state. Nobody notices until a rare double release or hang shows up in the field.
refuted.argument: This bug has exactly that shape: ReleaseAuxProcessResources() reset some state for reuse and missed the hash slots (message #1). v4 turns that pattern into a public operation in message #7, so each future change to the owner struct has one more place to keep correct. The README hunk states only a precondition and no check, and the material does not say what Reset asserts or verifies. Andres asked for "a helper that makes a resowner reusable after some assertions" in message #4.
refuted.author_must_show: Which assertions in ResourceOwnerReset() fail loudly in a cassert build when an owner is not fully empty, or when a field was not restored?

critic.reasoning: The reuse code exists today in ReleaseAuxProcessResources(), so v4 adds no new place to maintain. It moves that code into the generic resowner code, as Andres Freund asked in message #4. The assertion question survives in standards-compat-2.

refuted.title: Stable-branch fix differs from the master API, with no plan stated
refuted.failure_scenario: The bug exists back to 17, and the CommitFest entry targets stable. If v4 goes only to master and a v1-style local memset goes to 17 and later, resowner.c differs across branches in the code that handles release. Later backpatched resowner fixes then need separate versions per branch, and a missed difference can reintroduce the bug.
refuted.argument: v1 carried "Backpatch-through: 17", but v4 adds an exported function and changes release behavior for all owners (message #7). The thread does not say which version goes to back branches. Adding a symbol in a minor release is possible, but a committer would likely ask whether the sort and release clearing alone is the backpatch, with Reset kept for master only.
refuted.author_must_show: Which exact change do you propose for 17 and later, and how does it differ from the master commit?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which asks the same back-branch question with a more concrete failure scenario.

refuted.title: ResourceOwnerReset() duplicates delete and re-create of the owner
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension author sees two ways to reuse an owner: ResourceOwnerDelete() followed by ResourceOwnerCreate(), or the new ResourceOwnerReset(). Each later change to owner state, such as new fields or new per-kind storage, must also be restored correctly in Reset. A missed field shows up only when a reused owner misbehaves, as in this bug.
refuted.argument: Postgres already supports making a fresh owner: release all three phases, call ResourceOwnerDelete(), then call ResourceOwnerCreate(). The auxiliary path could do that and update CurrentResourceOwner, at the cost of one allocation per cleanup, which is not on a hot path. Andres Freund asked for a generic helper in message #4, and the author compares Reset to MemoryContextReset in message #5. Rahila Syed in message #6 preferred clearing entries in place over a new API, and the only measured benefit of keeping storage is for owners that are not deleted.
refuted.author_must_show: What does ResourceOwnerReset() give auxiliary processes that delete and re-create cannot, and does the stable-branch fix need the new API at all?

critic.reasoning: Auxiliary processes already reuse their owner today, so v4 exposes an existing operation and adds no second way. Andres Freund asked for the generic helper in message #4. The back-branch part is covered by standards-compat-1.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: v4 adds the exported function ResourceOwnerReset() to src/include/utils/resowner.h.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets stable and v1 said "Backpatch-through: 17", but v4 adds a public function.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A public reset operation in resowner.c must stay correct as the owner's state changes.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: ResourceOwnerSort() and bulk release now clear hash slots for every owner, not only auxiliary ones.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which part of v4 goes to stable branches, and can the back-branch fix work without adding ResourceOwnerReset() to resowner.h?
What does ResourceOwnerReset() do in a build without assertions when the owner or a child still holds resources or has not finished all three release phases?
How does clearing during sort and bulk release perform for transactions that hold many hashed resources of several kinds?
How does ResourceOwnerReset() fit with Rahila Syed's proposal to release all three phases in one call?

committability.owner_note: Andres Freund asked in message #4 for the generic helper and for clearing in ResourceOwnerSort(). The owner must know resowner.c and the auxiliary-process cleanup path.
committability.liability: The owner signs for changed release behavior in every resource owner on all branches that get the fix, and for a new public C function that extensions may call from then on.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 the same day as the first review and reached v4 with benchmarks within the thread, which suggests continued engagement.

priority.reason: The patch is about 12 KiB and local to resowner.c and its test module. It fixes a double release or hang in reused auxiliary owners, and the remaining points are a back-branch plan and the reset precondition check.

provisional_note: Without the code, I could not check what ResourceOwnerReset() asserts, or whether clearing slots before the release callbacks is safe when a callback errors. The benchmarks cover one resource kind and one pgbench workload.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: ResourceOwner refactoring
precedents_retrieved.summary: Heikki Linnakangas proposed replacing the per-kind arrays in ResourceOwner with one generic store: a small linear-searched array for recent entries plus a hash table for older ones. Each entry carries a kind with Release and PrintLeakWarning callbacks, so extensions can track their own resources the same way built-in code does.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier closed the entry because the latest patch no longer applied and had been waiting on author for weeks. Benchmarks in the thread showed the worst case still 24% slower than unpatched, and Aleksander Alekseev asked whether ResourceOwnerReleaseAll() could loop forever on the same entry. Neither question got an answer in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The latest patch does not apply anymore, and has been waiting on
author for a couple of weeks now, so switched as RwF for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: ResourceOwner refactoring
precedents_retrieved.summary: Refactor ResourceOwner so that all tracked resource kinds share one small linear-searched array plus an overflow hash table, in place of a separate array per kind. Each kind defines Release and PrintLeakWarning callbacks, so extensions can track their own resources the way built-in code does, and lookups such as catcache references get faster.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer objected to the design, and Aleksander Alekseev marked the patch set Ready for Committer in November 2021. In January 2022 the second patch no longer applied because of a conflict on resowner_private.h, and Julien Rouhaud set the entry to Waiting on Author. The visible messages show no rebase after that before the entry was returned. An earlier version had also been returned in October 2021 for the same reason.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The 2nd patch doesn't apply anymore due to a conflict on
resowner_private.h: http://cfbot.cputube.org/patch_36_3364.log.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid use of TopMemoryContext for resource owner cleanup in portals
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the freeing of failed portals' subsidiary memory contexts in At(Sub)Abort_Portals to after ResourceOwnerRelease during transaction abort. Resource owner cleanup code could then use memory below the portal, such as the executor context, so LLVM JIT, WaitEventSet and OpenSSL would no longer need TopMemoryContext allocations.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas held that anything needed for resource owner cleanup should live in TopMemoryContext, or in a dedicated child context of it. Under that rule, resource owners and memory contexts can be released in any order. He said the patch would add a hidden ordering dependency and make crashes more likely if a resource owner is released after its memory context is deleted. The author agreed to document the existing rule in the resource owner README.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think it's a good rule that anything that's needed for resource owner cleanup must be allocated in TopMemoryContext, so that there's no hidden dependency between resource owners and memory contexts and you can release them in any order.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix off-by-one in logical slot resource retention
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes the resource retention logic for logical slots, which treats confirmed_flush as inclusive while the rest of the code, including the decoding start point, treats it as exclusive. Two further patches clean up logical walsender init and add explanatory comments and docs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patches went stale and the author stopped responding. A reviewer reported that patches 0002 and 0003 no longer applied and asked for a rebase. No rebase followed, so the entry stayed in Waiting on Author for the whole commitfest and was returned with feedback. No objection to the fix itself appears in the thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since this patch has been in Waiting for Author state for the duration of the
commitfest without moving, I’m marking it Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: base backup client as auxiliary backend process
precedents_retrieved.summary: The postmaster starts an auxiliary process that takes a base backup from the primary when it finds a basebackup.signal file in a minimal data directory created by initdb, then continues startup in standby mode. Connection settings come from postgresql.conf, so setting up a standby no longer needs pg_basebackup.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry because he could not finish it, and said the order of startup actions in postmaster.c needed more thinking. Andres Freund's review had questioned the polling wait loop in PostmasterMain, missing error and signal handling in the base backup process, the handling of shutdown during the backup, and putting the backup code in libpqwalreceiver.c. Some refactoring parts were committed separately.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Unsurprisingly, the sequencing of startup actions in postmaster.c is
extremely tricky and needs more thinking.

precedents_retrieved.title: CREATEROLE and role ownership hierarchies
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set reduces what the CREATEROLE attribute allows and adds role ownership, so each role has an owner and non-superuser creators manage only the subtree of roles they own. After upgrade, the bootstrap superuser owns all existing roles, and REASSIGN OWNED and ALTER ROLE OWNER TO move ownership.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers did not agree on role ownership as the model. They objected that an owner would bypass most privilege checks on the roles it owns, and preferred building on SQL-standard ADMIN OPTION with separate grants that a superuser can revoke from creators. With no agreement and v15 too close, only the removal of the session-user self-administration exception was committed. Robert Haas proposed returning the entry, since later work might not take this form.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Stephen's, and now my, issue with ownership is that, since it implies
DAC, most checks will be bypassed for the owner.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow cluster owner to bypass authentication
precedents_retrieved.summary: A connection over a Unix-domain socket whose local effective OS user is the same as the server's effective user is accepted at once, without checking pg_hba.conf, and an option turns this off. The patch was meant as a first step before changing the initdb default authentication to md5 or SCRAM for both local and host connections.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut withdrew it and David Steele marked it Returned with feedback, because the discussion of a new default security configuration did not reach consensus. Stephen Frost objected that bypassing pg_hba.conf skips safeguards and audit trails, and that getpeerid() does not show the client has the same access as the server. Tom Lane and Stephen Frost preferred building this behavior into username maps (pg_ident.conf) instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It appears that the whole discussion of what a new default security
configuration could or should be hasn't really moved to a new consensus,
so given the time, I think it's best that we leave things as they are
and continue the exploration at some future time.

precedents_retrieved.title: Safer hash table initialization macro
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a macro, HASH_ELEM_INIT, that sets keysize and entrysize from a named key member and checks at compile time that the key is the first member of the entry struct. The thread grew into a larger patch series by Jelte Fennema-Nio with new hash table creation functions (hash_make and variants), automatic string or blob key detection, and a foreach_hash iteration macro.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible messages are positive reviews and fixes from late January 2026, and no message shows the withdrawal or a deciding objection.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P1] and [P2] are the earlier ResourceOwner refactoring that added the hash store, and they were returned only because the patches stopped applying, which does not apply here. Message #6 points to a separate proposal to release all three phases in one call, a related API change rather than an earlier attempt at owner reset.
The patch has no SQL, GUC, catalog, pg_dump or psql surface. The two objections above cover the only compatibility contracts I found: the stable-branch ABI and the C API naming.

The proposal changes only in-memory, per-backend resource owner state: no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, replication or wire-protocol changes. Adding ResourceOwnerReset() to resowner.h adds a symbol and does not change any existing signature, and the ResourceOwner struct is private to resowner.c, so a back-branch version would not break extension ABI.

The proposal changes internal resource owner bookkeeping and adds a C-level reset function. It adds no SQL-callable surface outside the test module, no privilege, no new data exposure and no path for unprivileged users. The bug it fixes involves double release of resources, so it improves safety more than it weakens it.
The core fix is local to resowner.c. Andres Freund, who knows this area, shaped the design, and the measured hot-path cost for non-users is small. That lowers the fit concerns.
The bug fix itself, clearing stale slots in ResourceOwnerSort() and bulk release, has no existing alternative in core. Only the new public Reset API overlaps with delete and re-create.

This is a bug fix for a real defect: a reused auxiliary owner can release resources twice or hang in ResourceOwnerAddToHash() (messages #1 and #3), and nobody disputed that. The new ResourceOwnerReset() has one caller today, but a committer who knows the area asked for a generic helper (message #4), so its demand is a design question for other angles.
